articleHeadline: Myanmar issues preventive guidelines for El Niño health risks
articleSummary: Myanmar, 20 October 2026: The Ministry of Health issued preventive guidelines to reduce health risks linked to El Niño. Water scarcity and flooding can contaminate supplies, elevating risks of diarrhea, dysentery, food poisoning, typhoid, hepatitis, and skin or eye infections; prevention emphasizes boiled or purified water, freshly cooked meals, avoiding food exposed to flies, and frequent handwashing with soap. Mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue fever and malaria can be reduced by eliminating breeding grounds, tightly covering water storage, and sleeping under treated nets. Hot, dry conditions raise wildfire, dust, and smoke risks, potentially triggering asthma and respiratory infections; wear masks during heavy dust or smoke, keep indoor air clean, and heed wildfire alerts.

articleSummary: Thailand confirms its first human case of parrot fever (psittacosis) in a bird owner in Bangkok.
